description.summary: private protocol between the Desilium compositor and its desktop shell

protocol.description:
This protocol lets the desktop shell (top bar, dock, launcher, window switcher) observe and control the compositor. It covers what layer-shell cannot express: the window list, workspaces, output geometry, compositor key bindings handed to the shell, and visual effects behind the shell's own layer surfaces.
The global is only advertised to trusted clients; see docs/shell-protocol.md. The shell being absent or crashing is a normal state for the compositor.
Batching: the compositor groups related changes and ends each group with a done event. A client should apply the state received since the previous done event atomically. Each toplevel handle has its own done event that ends a group of property events for that handle; the manager done event ends the whole update (new handles, closed handles, workspaces, output).
Versioning: new requests, events, enum entries and error codes may be added in later versions. A client must ignore unknown state values in the state array and unknown shortcut names.

interface.name: desilium_shell_manager_v1

description.summary: entry point for the desktop shell

interface.description: The manager announces windows, workspaces and the output, and accepts workspace and effect requests. When it is bound, the compositor sends the complete current state followed by a done event, and from then on only the changes, each batch followed by a done event.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Protocol errors are fatal for the connection. Values that merely become stale (for example a workspace index that no longer exists after the workspace count shrank) are never errors; the request is ignored.

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface is not a layer surface

entry.name: invalid_rectangle
entry.summary: a rectangle has a negative size

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops all updates. Existing toplevel handles stay valid until they are destroyed, but receive no further events. Effects set through set_surface_effects stay in place until their surface is destroyed.

request.name: switch_workspace
request.description: Makes the workspace with the given zero-based index the active one. Ignored when the index is out of range.

request.name: set_surface_effects

description.summary: ask for effects behind a layer surface

request.description:
Asks the compositor to draw a backdrop blur and/or rounded corners for the given layer surface of this client. The effects replace any earlier ones for the surface; all zeros removes them. The compositor clamps every value to 0..64 and may ignore the request when it cannot render the effect. The effects are dropped when the surface is destroyed.
The corners are in surface-local logical pixels and describe the shape of the visible panel (the blur and the clip follow it).

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: a layer surface of this client

arg.name: blur_radius
arg.summary: backdrop blur radius in logical pixels

event.name: toplevel
event.description: A new window exists. The handle is followed by its window_id, title, app_id, state and workspace events and a done event. Sent once per window for the lifetime of this manager.

event.name: workspaces

description.summary: workspace count or active workspace changed

event.description: Sent on bind and whenever the number of workspaces or the active workspace changes. The active index is always smaller than the count.

arg.name: active
arg.summary: zero-based index of the active workspace

event.name: output_geometry
event.description: Sent on bind and whenever the output, its scale or its work area changes. All rectangles are in logical pixels in the compositor's global space. The work area is the output minus the exclusive zones of layer surfaces (the area maximized windows fill).

event.name: shortcut

description.summary: a key binding owned by the shell was pressed

event.description: The compositor handled a key binding that the shell is meant to act on, for example "toggle_launcher". Unlike the state events this one is not batched and is not repeated on bind. Unknown names must be ignored.

event.name: done
event.description: All events since the previous done event form one consistent state.

interface.name: desilium_toplevel_handle_v1

description.summary: a window known to the shell

interface.description: A handle for one window. Property events are only sent when a value changed (and all of them on creation), each group ends with done. After the closed event the handle is inert and the client should destroy it.

enum.name: state

description.summary: window states reported in the state array

enum.description: Unknown values must be ignored. A minimized window is never reported as activated, maximized or fullscreen.

entry.name: minimized
entry.summary: the window is hidden to the dock

entry.name: maximized
entry.summary: the window fills the work area

request.name: activate
request.description: Switches to the window's workspace, restores the window if it is minimized, raises and focuses it.

request.name: close
request.description: The application decides whether it closes.

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: move the window to a workspace

request.description: Ignored when the index is out of range.

request.name: set_geometry

description.summary: place the window at a rectangle

request.description: Moves and resizes the window to the given rectangle in the compositor's global space, clamped to the work area of the window's workspace. Used to restore a saved layout. Like a snap, the window remembers its previous floating rectangle. Ignored for minimized windows and for rectangles of zero size.

request.name: set_minimize_rectangle

description.summary: tell where the window's dock icon is

request.description: The compositor animates minimizing towards this rectangle. The rectangle is relative to the top-left of the given layer surface of the shell (the compositor follows the surface if it moves). A null surface clears the rectangle. A zero-sized rectangle is allowed and means a point.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: layer surface holding the icon, or null to clear

event.name: window_id
event.description: Identifies the window for the lifetime of the compositor. The same window always has the same id, also across several manager objects, and ids are not reused. Sent first, once.

event.name: state
event.description: The array holds uint32 values of the state enum, each at most once.

description.summary: the window moved to another workspace

event.name: geometry
event.description: Position and size of the window in the compositor's global space, in logical pixels. Sent when the window is added and whenever it moves or is resized. Panels use it to dodge windows.

event.name: closed
event.description: Always followed by done. No further events follow.

description.summary: end of a group of property events for this window
